messages.author: afc5d1777b0456fc
messages.subject: How to profiling in rstan
parts:
Dear Stan users,

I would like to profile my stan model, and understand which C-level operations are time consuming.

I am not familiar with command lines but followed this approach:

% setenv LD_PROFILE mymodel.so
rstudio (wd: ~) # this is the command line output

Then I don't know what to do, should I run my stan() function in rstudio and type some more commands?

p.s. I don't have admin access so I cannot use oprofile commands..

Thanks for any input,
Craig

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to profiling in rstan
parts:
You might find it better to use CmdStan to profile Stan.
Much less going on and RStan's just a relatively thin
wrapper around R's memory and Stan. The time's still all
spent in computing gradients. So if you want to optimize,
that's where to put your attention.

- Bob
